reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource context, full StructureDefinition report, deterministic aggregate, and checked the behavior reports for findings whose `affectedResources` include `CoverageEligibilityResponse`. The review treats shared `Resource` and `DomainResource` behavior as context only because this assigned artifact is neither base resource.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 CoverageEligibilityResponse was trial-use/FMM 2, so there is not a normative or high-FMM presumption against change. The financial-management workflow is still business and audit relevant, so the review does not dismiss local compatibility loss merely because the resource was trial-use.

overall.oneLineConclusion: CoverageEligibilityResponse keeps the same resource identity and has no hard R4-to-R6 instance break, so migration is localized rather than a whole-resource program.

reasoning.thesisMd: The resource remains `CoverageEligibilityResponse` with the same canonical URL, DomainResource base, core reference targets, modifier flags, and local invariant shape. The R4-to-R6 direction is mostly stable: no R4 instance pattern identified in the report becomes structurally invalid solely because of this resource's local R6 changes.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The real migration shape is a set of local mixed-version and tooling chores. R6 responses may omit the formerly mandatory `request`, may carry new optional `event`, `statusReason`, and `error.expression` data, may expose `error.code` in summary views, and use `markdown` rather than `string` for `insurance.item.description`. Those changes require downgrade policy, generated-model refresh, terminology metadata refresh, and UI/rendering review, but they do not amount to a resource split, replacement, broad element rename, or unavoidable R4-to-R6 transform for ordinary R4 instances.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because a resource-level migration program is not already unavoidable, additional avoidable breaking changes should not be discounted as harmless. The current findings are mostly proportionate local changes, but the proper standards posture is still to preserve compatibility per change where that can be done without undermining the R6 design goal.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest possible less-breaking alternatives are limited. Keeping `request` mandatory would preserve R4 guarantees but would defeat the R6 ability to respond without a FHIR request resource. Modeling `event` only as an extension would improve R4 round-tripping but would lose first-class R6 validation and model support. Retaining or explicitly aliasing the old `remittance-outcome` canonical could reduce tooling churn, but the code values appear unchanged and the new name is semantically better. Keeping `description` as `string` would be less disruptive for generators but would not give renderers and validators a computable markdown signal.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: No direct OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP behavior finding was found for `CoverageEligibilityResponse`. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings remain relevant to general FHIR server/client migration, especially generic operations and shared search metadata, but they are not CoverageEligibilityResponse-specific resource-shape pressure.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate that major migration is `No`, that there are no hard or potential hard local R4-to-R6 instance breaks, and that shared base behavior should not be scored against this resource. I differ slightly in framing: instead of `low-material-change` and `no-special-break-avoidance-needed`, I classify the resource as mostly stable with local breaks and recommend per-change compatibility preservation, because the request relaxation, event addition, and markdown/tooling changes are concrete enough for implementers even though they do not force a whole-resource migration program.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for structural deltas because the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions were directly compared. Remaining uncertainty is about official committee rationale and terminology expansion details, especially for the outcome and benefit binding changes.

findingConsiderations.title: CoverageEligibilityResponse.request is no longer mandatory in R6
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the most important local compatibility change. It is not an R4-to-R6 invalidation, but it removes an R4 guarantee that responses link to a request, creating R6-to-R4 and mixed-version audit/reconciliation work. It is proportionate because preserving the old guarantee would block the apparent R6 use case.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds CoverageEligibilityResponse.event with required event details when present
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The optional `event` backbone is first-class new business timing content. It does not break R4 instances moving forward, but R6-to-R4 downgrade can lose event type/date information. This is a localized migration policy concern rather than evidence of a broad resource remodel.

findingConsiderations.title: insurance.item.description changes primitive type from string to markdown
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The JSON property remains string-valued and ordinary R4 text should remain acceptable, but generators, primitive wrappers, renderers, and sanitization paths can change. This should be handled as implementation tooling and UI-safety migration, not as a standards-level remodel.

findingConsiderations.title: CoverageEligibilityResponse.outcome required binding moved from remittance-outcome to eligibility-outcome
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The required binding canonical changes, but local evidence shows the same four code values. This matters for terminology caches, generated enums, profiles, and tests; it does not appear to reject old values. A published equivalence note would be low-cost helpful context, but the finding does not justify resource-level migration pressure.

findingConsiderations.title: Three benefit-related bindings strengthen from example to preferred
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Preferred bindings can create warning-level pressure in QA tooling, but they do not make local payer benefit codes invalid. This is a terminology-governance and warning policy update rather than an avoidable hard break.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds summary element CoverageEligibilityResponse.statusReason
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This optional summary field can be lost on downgrade to R4, but it does not change the underlying modifier `status` value and does not create forward migration pressure. It is a small additive local migration chore.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds CoverageEligibilityResponse.error.expression for locating implicated elements
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The field adds useful repair guidance and may require an extension for R4 downgrade, but losing it does not change the error code itself. It is auxiliary and optional.

findingConsiderations.title: CoverageEligibilityResponse.error.code is now included in summary views
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The element's path, type, cardinality, and binding remain stable. Only summary projection behavior changes, so this is a narrow API/projection awareness issue rather than an instance migration break.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource/DomainResource search metadata issue may affect generic clients that also process CoverageEligibilityResponse, but it is not a finding on the CoverageEligibilityResponse resource shape or a direct behavior finding assigned to this resource.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 core removes the Resource $meta operation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Generic Resource operation changes are real API migration context, but they should be resolved in the base Resource behavior review rather than counted as CoverageEligibilityResponse-specific migration pressure.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Document cross-version handling for R6 responses that omit `request` or populate `event`, `statusReason`, or `error.expression`, including whether R4 downgrades use extensions, data-loss warnings, or local synthesis.

Refresh generated models, terminology metadata, and UI rendering paths for the `markdown` description type, the `eligibility-outcome` binding canonical, preferred benefit bindings, and summary inclusion of `error.code`.

If standards text is being polished, add migration notes or explicit equivalence guidance for the outcome value set rename and the rationale for making `request` optional; no resource-level redesign appears necessary.

caveats: No official R4-to-R6 diff or committee rationale was available locally for this resource.
Terminology judgments rely on local CodeSystem/ValueSet evidence rather than authoritative R4 and R6 expansions.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were reviewed as context only and not scored as CoverageEligibilityResponse-specific findings.
